title: 6. Special Planet Facts (VERY HIGH EXAM VALUE)

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Venus is known as Earth's Twin, the Brightest Planet, and the Morning/Evening Star due to its atmospheric density and high reflectivity.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system, boasting the fastest rotation period (approx. 10 hours) and the largest moon, Ganymede.
Mars is nicknamed the Red Planet due to iron oxide on its surface and hosts Olympus Mons, the solar system's tallest volcano.
Saturn is surrounded by a prominent ring system and possesses the lowest density of all planets, lower than the density of water.
Venus and Uranus exhibit retrograde rotation, turning from East to West, unlike the other six planets.

blocks.content: Venus and Uranus rotate from east to west (clockwise), whereas all other planets rotate from west to east.

rows: Hottest planet; rotates clockwise (East to West)
Contains Olympus Mons & moons Phobos and Deimos
Fastest rotation; home to largest moon Ganymede
Density lower than water (0.69 g/cm³); home to Titan

items: Venus is hotter than Mercury despite being farther from the Sun due to a runaway greenhouse effect caused by dense carbon dioxide.
Saturn has a density of 0.69 g/cm³, making it the only planet that would theoretically float on water.
Phobos and Deimos are the two natural satellites of Mars, frequently tested in competitive examinations.
